answer: Overlap-scaled transaction surcharge. Each identity pays a base fee multiplied by 1 + 25 × (shared-neighbor fraction)², sampled from recent counterparties; overlap with an existing identity raises the multiplier. A fresh identity can sit in a low-overlap haven only while its graph is independent. Drawing counterparties from the same lagoon compounds the surcharge across the cluster. To shed that sybil plume, the attacker must route at least half its volume through unrelated agents, paying external spreads and latency; at 80% overlap the per-identity cost is 17× base.
